arms.name: Upper Arm
arms.summary: The Upper Arm is a strong anchor for whole-lake context, especially for long-term clarity, nutrient, and open-water bloom trends.
priorityQuestions: Are basin-wide bloom drivers intensifying before shoreline impacts emerge?
How closely do satellite signals match in-water measurements here?

arms.name: Lower Arm
arms.summary: The Lower Arm should emphasize recreation, nearshore exposure, and public communication because it matters most for day-to-day community use.
priorityQuestions: Which shoreline sites are repeatedly crossing health-relevant thresholds?
How quickly do public-facing conditions change after heat, wind, or inflow events?

arms.name: Oaks Arm
arms.summary: The Oaks Arm deserves special treatment because it combines narrow geometry, shoreline use, cyanotoxin concerns, and distinct water-quality pressures.
priorityQuestions: Can the dashboard distinguish between persistent local severity and lake-wide episodes?
Which upstream or seasonal factors appear most predictive for extreme toxin conditions?

sources.name: CLAMP Monthly Monitoring
sources.summary: Monthly physical, chemical, and biological lake monitoring that continues the older DWR ambient record across the three Clear Lake arms.
sources.mvpUsage: Core trend charts and arm comparison
sources.automationNote: Likely feasible through CEDEN extracts and portal downloads, but the county portal needs contract validation.

sources.name: Tribal Cyanotoxin Monitoring
sources.owner: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians
sources.summary: Shoreline and interior toxin monitoring focused on cyanobacteria impacts, with current results plus historical material from 2014 through 2024.
sources.mvpUsage: Risk map, toxin severity panel, historical hotspots
sources.automationNote: Very valuable source. We should expect some custom extraction or partnership work for reliable automation.

sources.name: FHABS Incident And Results Data
sources.summary: Statewide freshwater harmful algal bloom reports, cases, responses, and results in California Open Data with advisory context.
sources.automationNote: Strong candidate for scheduled ETL once the CKAN resource endpoints are confirmed directly.

sources.name: California Satellite HAB Map
sources.summary: Satellite-derived cyanobacteria and chlorophyll-a estimates that help add lake-wide spatial context between field samples.
sources.mvpUsage: Spatial map layer and trend overlays
sources.machineReadableStatus: Tool available, API path to confirm
sources.automationNote: Useful for map overlays and model features, but should remain clearly labeled as supplemental rather than definitive.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap Clear Lake Geometry
sources.summary: Public OSM multipolygon geometry for the Clear Lake shoreline, used as a geographic context layer under monitoring pins.
sources.mvpUsage: Map shoreline geometry and public spatial context
sources.machineReadableStatus: Overpass API extract cached as static JSON
sources.automationNote: Use cached extracts and visible OSM/ODbL attribution; do not call Overpass from every public page view.

sources.name: USGS Tributaries And Lake Levels
sources.summary: Hydrology and watershed-monitoring resources that can supply inflow, streamflow, and lake-level drivers for both the dashboard and the future model.
sources.automationNote: Best early live feed candidate because the service surface is mature and designed for automation.

sources.name: Local Weather Backbone
sources.summary: Planned local-first weather and soil sensing backbone that can provide reviewed hyperlocal context for rainfall, wind, heat, and station health near Clear Lake.
sources.coverage: Private/local stations first; public context exports later
sources.mvpUsage: Weather context for lake-condition interpretation, not direct lake-health determination
sources.automationNote: Target a schema-governed weather-context.json export with explicit units, staleness thresholds, station metadata, and public/private field boundaries.

sources.name: CEDEN Chemistry Data
sources.summary: State environmental exchange network with chemistry results that can support historical trends, parameter selection, and arm-level backfill.
sources.mvpUsage: Backfill, QA checks, and long historical context
sources.automationNote: Excellent for durable ingestion, though filtering and data quality handling need care.

modules.title: Lake Overview
modules.body: Show the three arms as distinct monitoring zones with quick summaries of coverage, latest known update windows, and source confidence.

modules.title: Monitoring Map
modules.body: Plot shoreline and open-water sites, then layer current toxin context, satellite context, and advisory history without blending unlike signals.

modules.title: Trend Explorer
modules.body: Let the public compare temperature, chlorophyll-a, nutrients, toxin results, and seasonal behavior by arm and by source.

modules.title: Data Notebook
modules.body: Document every source, cadence, caveat, and retrieval method so the dashboard is useful to residents, journalists, and researchers.

modules.title: Field And Microscopy Intake
modules.body: Future authenticated entry for lakeside observations, sample metadata, and freshwater phytoplankton identifications from light microscopy, with QA review before public display or model training.

guardrails.title: Do Not Overstate Freshness
guardrails.body: Every chart and map should show the observation date, not just the publication date, because these feeds update on different schedules.

guardrails.title: Keep Satellite Data Supplemental
guardrails.body: Satellite-derived cyanobacteria and chlorophyll-a estimates add spatial reach, but they should not be presented as direct public-health determinations.

guardrails.title: Separate Conditions From Forecasts
guardrails.body: Observed toxin measurements, public advisories, and model-generated bloom outlooks should stay visibly distinct to avoid false precision.

guardrails.title: Preserve Community Trust
guardrails.body: Tribal monitoring and local county monitoring should be credited clearly and represented without flattening away their different purposes.

guardrails.title: Review Field Data Before Publication
guardrails.body: Student, volunteer, or NOAA-associated field and microscopy records should remain in a reviewed intake layer until sample custody, location precision, taxonomic confidence, and permission-to-publish status are documented.

phases.name: Phase 1
phases.goal: Ship a public MVP with a source catalog, lake map shell, and trend views powered by cleaned static extracts.
deliverables: Arm-level charts using seed data extracts

phases.name: Phase 2
phases.goal: Automate ingestion for the most stable public feeds and add source freshness indicators to the site.

phases.name: Phase 3
phases.goal: Stand up an internal forecasting pipeline that predicts arm-level bloom severity while keeping uncertainty explicit.

phases.name: Stretch Goal
phases.goal: Add a reviewed field-data intake workflow for lakeside sampling and freshwater phytoplankton microscopy records.
deliverables: QA review queue before public release
Export path for approved observations and future ML features

mlRoadmap.title: Prediction Target
mlRoadmap.body: Start with weekly Low, Moderate, and High severity labels by arm, based on toxin concentrations and advisory-relevant thresholds rather than trying to predict every raw measurement.

mlRoadmap.title: Feature Families
mlRoadmap.body: Use lagged toxin values, chlorophyll-a, nutrients, temperature, dissolved oxygen, lake level, tributary inflow, weather, seasonality, and satellite signals when they are aligned in time.

mlRoadmap.title: Modeling Discipline
mlRoadmap.body: Validate with rolling time splits, compare against a simple seasonal baseline, and publish uncertainty notes so the model is framed as decision support rather than certainty.

mlRoadmap.title: Responsible Release
mlRoadmap.body: Expose early forecasts only as experimental outputs with model date, training window, input summary, uncertainty notes, and public-health disclaimer language.
